title: Attack and defend: ransomware
blurb: Follow a ransomware intrusion through the kill chain, find where each control could have stopped it, and plan the recovery.
purpose: Ransomware is the attack most organizations fear. In this lab you follow an intrusion through each stage, see where each Cisco control could have stopped it, and learn the right order to respond and recover.
scenario: A file server's shares are suddenly full of files ending in **.locked**, and there's a ransom note in every folder. Walk back through how the attack unfolded, decide where Cisco controls would have broken the chain, and recover safely.
topology:
User laptop ── SW ── file server
   Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, FTD, Secure Network Analytics
objectives: Order the stages of a typical ransomware intrusion
Match a control to each stage
Contain and recover in the right order

steps.title: The kill chain
steps.learn: Modern ransomware is rarely a single click. Operators get in, spread, steal data for **double extortion**, and only encrypt at the end. That leaves several chances to stop them.
steps.question: Order from first to last.
items: Initial access: a phishing attachment runs a loader on a laptop
Command and control: the loader beacons out to the operator's server
Credential theft and lateral movement to the file server
Encryption of the shares and the ransom note

steps.title: Break the chain
steps.learn: Each stage leaves different traces, so each is caught by a different tool.
steps.task: Match each stage to the Cisco control best placed to stop or detect it.

fields.label: Loader runs on the laptop
options: Umbrella (blocks the CnC domain at DNS)
Secure Network Analytics (unusual internal connections and data hoarding)
FTD (blocks SMB between user and server segments)

fields.label: Beacons to the operator's domain
options: Umbrella (blocks the CnC domain at DNS)
Secure Network Analytics (unusual internal connections and data hoarding)
FTD (blocks SMB between user and server segments)
fields.answer: Umbrella (blocks the CnC domain at DNS)

fields.label: Lateral movement from the laptop to servers
options: Umbrella (blocks the CnC domain at DNS)
Secure Network Analytics (unusual internal connections and data hoarding)
FTD (blocks SMB between user and server segments)
fields.answer: FTD (blocks SMB between user and server segments)

fields.label: Staging and uploading gigabytes of data
options: Umbrella (blocks the CnC domain at DNS)
Secure Network Analytics (unusual internal connections and data hoarding)
FTD (blocks SMB between user and server segments)
fields.answer: Secure Network Analytics (unusual internal connections and data hoarding)

steps.title: Respond in the right order
steps.learn: Contain first, so the attack stops spreading. Preserve evidence before you wipe anything. Restore only from backups you know are clean.
steps.task: Put the response steps in order.
steps.question: Order from first to last.
items: Isolate affected hosts (Secure Endpoint isolation, switch port shutdown)
Disable or reset the compromised accounts
Preserve evidence: memory, logs and a sample of the encrypted files
Rebuild or clean the systems and restore from offline, tested backups
Review the root cause and close the gaps

steps.title: Backups
steps.question: Why must at least one backup copy be offline or immutable?

options.text: Operators look for backups and encrypt or delete them first. A copy they can't reach or change is what makes recovery possible without paying.

options.why: They're often slower. Their value is that the attacker can't reach them.
It's the main technical defense against losing everything.

summary: The ransomware kill chain from phishing to encryption, Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, FTD segmentation and Secure Network Analytics placed at each stage, a contain-first response, and offline or immutable backups.
